{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and confirmed **19 findings**, of which **17 are compliant** and **2 are deviations**. Overall the paper is unusually favourable to us: indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), the licence grant (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), auto-renewal mechanics (§ 8), transition assistance (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all sit at our preferred position, and the Agreement contains no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or non-solicitation burden on us (§ 2.1, § 12.3).

Two issues are material and both fall into walk-away territory:

1. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7).** Late payment triggers liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week, compounding, and capable of exceeding the remaining contract value. This fails both our preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). We propose deleting the formula and replacing it with an express no-liquidated-damages statement; the disputed-amount and no-interest mechanics in § 7.3 are unaffected.

2. **Illusory liability cap (§ 21).** Section 21 is mutual and already carries our full preferred carve-out set, but "Fees" is defined at §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee stated in the first Order Form, and § 21.1 further confines the measure to that first Order Form. Each Party's aggregate liability is therefore effectively USD 12,000 — far below six months' fees and short of even the fallback. Two surgical edits cure this at the preferred level: reset the cap to the greater of lowercase fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000; and confirm that our payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. The favourable direct-damages language in § 21.2 stays verbatim.

Nothing else requires a redline. Where clauses fall marginally short of ideal wording we have noted the point rather than flagged it — see the notes column below.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 (§ 7.7) | 15% of annual Fees per week for late invoices; compounding, uncapped in practice. Walk-away. Replace with express no-liquidated-damages provision. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 | Cap basis is the defined "Fees" (USD 12,000 implementation fee, first Order Form only). Walk-away. Reset cap basis and 12-month lookback; carve out Customer payment obligations. |
| 3 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 | Preferred position in full; § 21.3 lists indemnification as an Excluded Claim, so the indemnity sits outside the § 21.1 cap. |
| 4 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 | Preferred. Noted only: ownership/licence conditioned on payment of Fees; § 13.3 permits narrow suspension for material uncured breach. |
| 5 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 | Preferred. Competitor bar is consent-gated rather than absolute — noted, not redlined. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 (§ 12.3; § 2.1) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us. § 12.4 restrains Vendor and benefits us. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 | Preferred; Affiliate and contractor coverage, perpetual paid-up licence, transferable under § 24. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 (§ 12.3) | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint on us. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 (§ 9.4; § 29.4) | 30 days' notice, accrued Fees only, prepaid refunds; no Vendor convenience right. Narrow "Fees" definition noted. |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 | Every preferred element met; no direct access to our systems. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 | New York law, exclusive New York County forum; CISG excluded. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12 (§ 12.3; § 7.6) | No MFN burden on us; § 7.6 MFN runs in our favour. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 (§ 2.1; § 12.3; § 7.1) | No minimum quantity, committed spend or shortfall mechanic. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 (§ 12.3) | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant on either Party. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 8 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI-U and 3%. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 | Up to six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion; expiring-Order-Form rates favour us. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 | Preferred; disclaimer in § 19.5 does not limit express warranties. Malicious-code warranty limited to code intentionally introduced by Vendor — noted. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 | All preferred limits met, including USD 5m cyber and privacy; certificates on request. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Both deviations are flagged as walk-away in the playbook and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** A weekly, compounding 15%-of-annual-Fees charge for a minor payment breach that can exceed remaining contract value. Our position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties; the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees) is also failed. We do not sign with this formula in place. There is no double-flag risk here — § 9.4 confirms only accrued Fees are owed on termination without cause, and § 27 termination is "without penalty".
2. **§ 21.1 — cap basis.** A cap of effectively USD 12,000 provides no meaningful recourse and falls below the six-month fallback. The carve-outs and mutuality in § 21 are already acceptable, so this is a narrow, two-edit fix rather than a rewrite of the section.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline with the two proposed changes only, prefixed **[Playbook]**, and explain in each comment what changed and why: (a) § 7.7 replaced with an express no-liquidated-damages provision; (b) § 21.1 cap reset to the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, with a confirmation that our payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
2. Confirm to the business that no other clause requires negotiation, so bandwidth can be concentrated on these two points.
3. Flag internally the narrow definition of "Fees" at §§ 1.5/1.6 (implementation fee only), which also softens the pro-rata refund language in §§ 9.4 and 10.2 and the warranty refund in § 19.4. This is not redlined under those rules, but the § 21 edit deliberately uses lowercase "fees paid or payable" to avoid inheriting the defined term; commercial should confirm the intended fee construct in the Order Forms.
4. Note for the file that the § 21 finding was recorded as verification "repaired"; we should re-confirm the final § 21 language against the executed Order Form fee figures before signature.
5. Escalate both walk-away items to the deal owner now so that, if Vendor refuses either, we have time to decide before the signature date.
"}
